utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik, please continue with your witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours. I should like to ask the usher to please move slightly the ELMO, because I cannot see the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Will you please tell me if you talked with somebody between yesterday and today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not talk to anybody between yesterday and today. Yes, I talked to somebody at the hotel; but regarding this case, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, please, according to the statement that -- of the statement that you gave to the police in your country, you reported for that interview on a Friday. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not remember the day, but it's possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And you were told to come back on Monday, and that you would make your statement then, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's true that I made an appointment. I came back a couple of days after.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And you spent the whole weekend thinking what and how you will talk about this and what kind of a statement you would make on that Monday. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whether it's correct that I had time to think, I don't know. I went to work on that weekend and came back after work, directly after work.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Is making a statement to the police an everyday routine, a common thing to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not a common thing for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So you say you were not worried. Once you made up your mind to make the statement, you didn't begin to worry about what kind of a statement you would be making, especially as you were told that that statement could be used against you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't say I was particularly worried. I just made my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, please: And you spoke freely, and you told them the whole and complete truth, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You gave the statement freely and spoke about everything that you knew. Is that it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And tell me: Whilst you talked to the police, or rather, the investigators of this Tribunal, as you put it, did you also speak freely, or did they ask you questions? Was it a question-and-answer method, or did you just talk freely?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a mixture of both.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Were certain -- did they try to put some words into your mouth, some thoughts and ideas?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wouldn't say that. They didn't, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: For instance, did they physically describe to you Tuta, as you call him? Did they describe the gentleman to you physically? Did they tell you what he looked like physically to jog your memory or something?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they asked me to describe him, and I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Uh-huh. Then, tell me, how is it -- if you said the whole truth in your first statement, how is it that you never once mentioned that Tuta, and you told them the whole and complete truth?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first statement that I gave was about the prisoners being used as human shields, and Tuta was not present during the attack where the prisoners were being used as shields. It came later, when the investigators asked me for the battalion command.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I'm not asking you -- I did not ask you what you have just told me. Of course I have no way of knowing what you had in your head when you made the statement, but the fact is that you never mentioned him. And later on, when you met with the investigators, you did say something about him. So I'm asking you about that police, and I did ask you a while ago whether it was the whole truth. And you said, yes, that you had told them the whole truth.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did tell the truth. What I told them was the truth, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Right. In March 1993, you said you left Denmark. When was that? Was it the middle of March or the end of March?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure. I don't remember. It was sometime in March.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Do you remember, when did you arrive in Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some like three days after I left the Danish border.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Was this still March or was it April by that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was still March.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And you stayed several days in Zagreb, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I stayed in Zagreb for approximately three days.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, you communicated in English whilst in Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was mostly in German.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And no sooner did you arrive in Zagreb than you looked for the police. Did you think that it was the police that you should report to as a volunteer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't sure where to report to, so I guess I just asked the policeman so that he could give me advice, where to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: In 1993, in April or March, was there a war in Zagreb, was Croatia at war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were no war actions in Zagreb, and I don't know if there was fighting going on down south. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So you introduced yourself to a policeman and said what was your objective, and he directs you to the Ministry of Defence straight away; is that how it was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. First he -- first he advised me to go to a police station, and he said that they would drive me to a place where I could sign up for the Croatian army.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And you asked to join the Croatian army, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And at the Ministry of Defence, they admitted you straight away, somebody saw you straight away, but they refused to enrol you in the Croatian army; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. They told me that the Croatian army were not taking any more foreigners within their ranks because they had a problem with the United Nations, doing that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And you knew that there were foreigners in the Croatian army before that; did you have that personal knowledge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I knew that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: In the statement that you gave to the police of your country, you said that Mr. Blazinovic saw you. And in a statement that you gave to the OTP, you said that he travelled with you and that he was a commander. Now, was he somebody working for the Ministry of Defence or was he a commander? Which one of these two things is true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a commander for the unit in Posavina/Orasje.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, that 1993, in March or April that year, were there any HOS members in Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did they wear their patches to show what forces they belonged to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I met a guy at the Ministry of Defence who was wearing a black uniform with a HOS patch on his left arm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Do you know, when was HOS disbanded in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, please, you then went to Orasje and spent six months there. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And after that, you went back to Zagreb and stayed in Zagreb a couple of days. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the whole time I stayed in Zagreb, but it's true I went to Zagreb from Orasje, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And from Zagreb, you went to Mostar. How long did it take you to reach Mostar? Were the roads open? And could you travel normally, as you liked, or did you have to take some roundabout routes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think we had to take some roundabouts, but it was quite easy to travel to Mostar. And it took me about 24 hours, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I calculated that time very well. And now I will ask you, you couldn't reach Mostar prior to the end of September. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you ask me when I reached Mostar or...?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yes, one could put it that way, but since I did my calculations, so my question is very simple: You couldn't make it to Mostar before the latter half of September. The earliest that you could get there was the latter part of the second half of September. I'm asking you if you remember that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the specific date I arrived in Mostar. I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: But you were in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in Mostar, yeah, late summer '93.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Late summer '93, you were not in Mostar then.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: When did you say, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: End of the summer. End of the summer '93, you could not be in Mostar then.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in Mostar late summer '93, yes. I don't remember the specific date, but it was somewhere late summer '93.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Both in the statement that you gave to the police of your country and the one that you gave to the OTP, you described identically your journey, you described identically the time intervals. And if one does a simple calculation, one sees that you could not have arrived in Mostar in late summer '93. So will you tell us what is true, the first statement, the second statement, or what you are telling us today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm telling nothing but the truth. And I was in Mostar in late summer '93. How you calculate, I don't know. But I was in Mostar late summer '93, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Very simple. Even if you had left Denmark on the 1st of March, you couldn't have got there before the 1st of September even if you had taken a plane, because you said that you spent six months in Orasje. And that's why I'm asking you that. I'm asking you if that's correct. Is your statement that you spent six months in Orasje correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I saw Mr. Prosecutor is standing.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Your Honour, it seems that the witness three times answered the Defence question, that in the late summer 1993 he was in Mostar. Whether you like it or not, the response is given. No need to repeat your questions several times. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Will the Prosecutor address his remarks to the Bench Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. and not to Defence counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: We don't want any quarrelling between counsel at any stage in this trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, it is true that the witness said that he was there in the late summer three times.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, with your leave, I will answer my colleague. And thank you, Your Honour, Judge Clark, for your intervention. I think that I'm following a very simple logic, because it transpires from the statement from this witness. I'm not making up anything, and this is the purpose of cross-examination. Your Honours, if I may, if somebody says in two statements that he spent six months somewhere, and then in a third statement says that he left in March, then one does very simple addition and arrives at a conclusion. And in the cross-examination, I'm entitled to check the truth of one's statement. He can repeat 20 times that it was -- he was there in late summer, but the conclusion -- but, well, we shall leave the conclusion for the future. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Krsnik, for intervening. Perhaps you could ask this witness what he means by late summer, and then we might get a month out of him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Please be so kind and tell us what do you mean when you say late summer in Mostar, in Denmark, to see the difference, if there is one.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if there's any difference from Denmark to Bosnia, but late summer, I mean, like August, September.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: By "late," would you include the latter, the second half of September in that definition of late summer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I guess so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You said that a soldier that you found there in Mostar or wherever you were, that there was no command structure, that it wasn't a proper army, that they were all either drunk or drugged. Did you also drink and take drugs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not. Yes, I had some drinks, but not on the front line, no. When I was off duty, yes, I had some beers with my friends.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And you never took any drugs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: In what language did you communicate in Mostar? How would you keep up with events?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometime it was pretty hard, but we mostly communicated in German, English, and then by interpreter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me: On the 17th of September, would you say it was the first or the second half of September?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 17th must be the second half of September, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, Mr. Naletilic's Defence has no further questions for this witness. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Par.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness Q. I'm Mr. Zelimir Par. I'm one of the counsel of Vinko Martinovic. Let's start off with March 1993. You said that it was then that you departed Denmark in order to join the war in Bosnia and Herzegovina, and you stated as your reason, your idealism, your sense of adventure, and your desire to fight the Serbs. Can you please tell us more specifically what ideals were you fighting for and why did you want to fight the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I saw -- from what I saw in the media, television, newspapers, it was -- the bad guy was the Serbs violating Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Did you have any particular position in regards of Croatia? Did you have any special ties, any relationship?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you also want to fight the Muslims? What was your position in regards of that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I arrived, the Croats and the Muslims were fighting together, at least in Posavina they were. But later on, there were hostilities between those two parts.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: And what was your attitude towards Muslims and Croats then? What happened to your ideals in the light of this conflict; did they change or did you just want to participate in a war, regardless of who was fighting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if my idealism changed. I think so, yes, after a while in the Croatian army. Things was not like they -- like they looked as when I left Denmark. Something -- it was just realism.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: So why didn't you go straight back to Denmark? Why did you decide to stay on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now I was in the army, and I felt like I have to do my duty, like everybody else in that army.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Now, you also mentioned this sense of adventure which also led you there. Was that based on a desire to make some money as a mercenary or perhaps reap some other benefits through some booty or any such thing? Were you thinking along those lines when you decided to join the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never went down to Croatia for the money. Already before I left Denmark, I knew that the foreign volunteers down there were not paid very well. It was not for the money, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Very well. Can you now please tell me what your motivation was to come here as a witness, to give evidence here? What motivated you to do that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I feel like what I was part of in Mostar, using prisoners as human shields, has nothing to do with soldiering. As I see it, a soldier in a western country wouldn't do that; not in my army, at least. Justice has to be done. That's my motivation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Very well. When you came back to Denmark from Croatia, did somebody from the police authorities or judicial authorities talk to you, have an interview with you, regarding the events in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Were you perhaps afraid that some court proceedings could be launched in respect of what you were involved in, in Mostar and Bosnia and Herzegovina, what you may have been involved in, so that you could have been also included in some of the proceedings in respect of those events?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never thought about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Let us go back to the tragic death of the five-year-old boy in the apartment in Mostar to which you testified yesterday. Are you aware that there was a police investigation about this incident in Mostar and that your friend Adolf was deported to Austria and then to Germany, where the court proceedings against him continued; do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know there was a police investigation, at least I saw police officers outside the apartment, but I'm not aware of what happened after that, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Do you know and did you see that after that incident, immediately after the death of that young boy, it was Stela in person who arrested this man, Adolf, and turned him over to the police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know that. I saw him at Stela's headquarter, where he was -- I couldn't see if he was arrested, but he was sitting there defending himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Were you also detained or arrested in connection with that incident and questioned by the police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Immediately after that incident, were all foreigners who were members of that unit relieved from their post in that unit; do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: In terms of time, how long was it between that incident and when you were let go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Approximately a month, ten days, a couple of months, shortly thereafter, long thereafter?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember it at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Very well. Later on - this is still in relation to this incident, the killing of this young boy - did you later learn that this boy was not an orphan at all but that his parents lived in your immediate neighbourhood, and that Stela personally organised the burial of this boy and helped finance it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Yesterday you mentioned a Danish citizen, whose name we agreed not to mention in this courtroom, who, along with you, was a member of that unit in Mostar. Did you see him after you had left Bosnia and Herzegovina? Were you in contact with him in this intervening period since you've left Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I spoke to him on the telephone a couple of times.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Can you recall approximately when it was that you last talked to him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's many months ago. I don't exactly remember when.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Did you tell him that you were going to give evidence before this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: We talked about -- he mentioned to me that he has been talking to some investigators, but we never talked about giving testimony in this Tribunal, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Did you tell him what you did: that you went to the police, that you responded to these proceedings by trying to contribute to finding the truth about it? Did you talk to him about this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I kept that to myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: There were other foreigners in this unit, Canadian and American citizens. You did not want to divulge their names, while you did reveal the names of the other foreign members of this unit. What was your reason for your protecting the names of these Canadians and Americans?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Both of them were close friends with me, we served in a unit together after all this in Mostar, and I don't want to involve them in any of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Of what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: This trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Why? What is bad about their being mentioned in this Tribunal, to be referred to? Why do you believe that this would be something unpleasant to them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm quite sure that no -- none of them would feel comfortable by coming here. I'm -- I just know that they wouldn't be comfortable doing this, I'm sure, and I don't want to involve them. If they want to do it, they have to come themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Very well. When you joined the Croatian army and the HVO, did you use your real name or did you use a false name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I used my own name, my real name.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Very well. Are you currently still a soldier, or can you tell us what you do now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, you understand that this witness is under a Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. pseudonym, so I advise you not to go into the very details which might identify this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think Your Honour understands the comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday, during the cross-examination, you said that after your return to Denmark, you had -- you experienced problems in readjusting to life in Denmark. And you were asked why it was -- why it took you six years to give a statement after your return. My question is, during the period of time of your readjustment, did you undergo any kind of therapy? Were you confined, perhaps, in any way? Maybe did you run afoul of the law? Did anything happen in those six years?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I received no therapy, no. I was in conflict with the law one time, that's true. I have been -- how you say, for violence. I spent 60 days in prison for beating up another man.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Can you tell me, do you speak any Croatian, or what languages do you use to communicate with people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under normal circumstances in Denmark or --

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Actually, I'm interested in Mostar. What did you use?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: English, German, and some Croatian. I speak a little, not much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: In the unit in which you served, who knew English and German? Who were the persons who spoke those languages and with whom you could communicate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't exactly remember the names, but there was one guy who spoke English quite good. We called him "Sky News." Us, the foreigners, we called him "Sky News."

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us turn to that unit a little bit. Can you tell us what size unit it was, how many men were in it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say 30, 35 men, just about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Did you know the command structure of this unit? Yesterday, you mentioned on several times -- several times that commanders were issuing some orders. So do you know anything about its command structure?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was very hard to tell if there was any structure in the unit, but I knew Stela was in command. And while you were doing front service, you were just listening, taking orders from the men who were giving them, mostly running around with a Motorola radio. That's just about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Very well. Yesterday, you were mentioning those officers -- in other words, they were just there issuing orders, but they didn't have any rank insignia or other insignia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Can you now tell us, what was the relation -- did the position of the command of the city of Mostar to Stela and his men? Do you know anything about the flow of orders from the city command to Stela?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Now, let me ask you this: Did this unit ever move from the positions which it held and which you showed us yesterday on the map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we never moved. Yes, from building to building. But we didn't move from the area, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Did this unit have the same task as other units who were deployed next to it, and what was that task?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think they had the same task as units next to them, and the task was holding the positions and the building to prevent that any enemy soldiers were passing through.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Very well. Now, let me ask you this: Were members of this unit persons who used to live in that neighbourhood before the war, or were these recruited convicts, as you pointed out at one point yesterday? Could you establish that through your direct communication with them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: The thing I said about that they were ex-convicts, that's one thing I was told. I was told that the Kasniske Bojna, punishment battalion, when the unit was formed, it mainly consisted of ex-cons from ex-Yugoslavia. But I guess that many of the members of the unit were living in the area of Mostar, the neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: When you say living there, were they always living there, or did they move there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how long time they lived or if they actually lived there. But there was some locals, that's for sure. I don't know if they moved to the area or lived there always. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Very well. Now, you mentioned prisoners who were held by the unit. Do you know how they came to be there? Did the unit take them prisoner and held them or what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how they got there, but -- whether they were civilians or whether they were ex-members of the Armija BiH, but they were prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Very well. Now, were these prisoners kept under some special watch? Were they tied? Where did they sleep; where were they fed? Can you try to tell us a little bit about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were not tied or locked up. They walked around free in the area. Where they did eat, I don't know. At the place, I guess.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Were prisoners allowed to go back to their families in town and then report back to the unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if they were allowed to do that. I didn't saw that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Yesterday, you said that you saw a case of torture on one of the prisoners, and one of your friends, (redacted) the mercenary, was beating a Muslim prisoner. My question to you is: Did you report this incident to anyone? Did you go to Stela or to some other commander and tell them that this had happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw this (redacted), who you're regarding as my friend, and I don't regard him as my friend. I didn't like him. No, I did not report that incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Very well. I'm sorry if I mentioned him as your friend and he was not. Could you distinguish between Croats and Muslims and Serbs in Mostar? Were you able to make such distinctions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whether there were any Serbs in Mostar, I don't know. But I could distinguish the Croats from the Muslim, the Muslims as prisoners and the enemy, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm afraid that I couldn't hear the interpretation. Very well, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Let us now go back to that action that you took part in, and let me ask you when this action took place. Can we try to narrow it more, in terms of when exactly it happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have any specific dates, but somewhere in the late summer, you know, '93.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: You said that a day before this action was to take place, somebody told you that there would be an attack, that the tanks and artillery would be used, that there would be wooden rifles that would be placed in the hands of prisoners. Who was it who told you this, and who else was present during that conversation, and where did the conversation take place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who it was, I don't have a name on him, but it was one of the guys who were in command at the front line, and the conversation took place at the front lines a couple of days before the attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: And who else was present there, somebody who could confirm this, with whom we could corroborate this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: The conversation went -- when it took place, there was us, the foreigners, were present. And the other Danish guy was present, for instance.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Can you tell me, in which language did the commander speak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't quite remember, but I think it was English. Maybe half English, half Croatian. I can't quite remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: A moment ago, there was a question, "Who spoke foreign languages in this unit?" You said that there was one person who spoke English well. Was that the person who told you these things?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't think that was the person. There were several guys speaking English, but the one I mentioned before was one of them who was speaking very good English, that you could actually have a conversation with him. But I don't remember if he was present during this conversation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: The commander who spoke to you, how did he speak English? Was he fluent, did he speak broken English, could you understand him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember. Maybe the interpreter was being used. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: I'm sure we'll be able to verify that. If there was one interpreter in the unit, there was one person who spoke English well, and do you refer to that person as the interpreter?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't refer to actually one person as an interpreter. Things were interpreted every day, but interpreting, good interpreting -- much of the conversations were like half German, half English, half Croatian, a mixture, you know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Did the name "Alen Nargilic" mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember a guy, a Croatian guy, named "Alen," yes, and he spoke rather good English, quite good English.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Was he perhaps the interpreter responsible for your group, for the group of foreigners?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no actual interpreter who was responsible for anything. If it was needed and if it was possible, things were just interpreted by somebody who could do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Very well. Just one more question about this. Was Alen Nargilic present at that conversation a day or two before the attack when the attack was discussed; do you remember that? Was he present there or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Was it he that you nicknamed "Sky News"? You said that one of them had a nickname "Sky News." Was he the one, was he the soldier who spoke well English?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he was not the one. The one called "Sky News," he was called "Sky News" because he had this flak jacket, like a flak vest, bulletproof or whatever, with a "Sky News" logo on it. It was a blue flak jacket with white "Sky News" logo in the front of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: And that "Sky News," was he present on that occasion; was he present at that conversation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, I do not recall who was present.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Thank you. Very well. Now, let's move on to that day, to the day of the attack. You say that you saw three prisoners then with some kind of wooden rifles. Did you know those three men? The prisoners, did you know them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure if I knew them. I really didn't have any kind of Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. personal relationships with any of these prisoners. Whether I knew them, I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Very well. Then on the basis of what do you claim that they were prisoners and that they were Muslims? How did you come to that conclusion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was said that Muslim prisoners were being used, and I guess they were Muslim prisoners. They were not Croatian, I can tell you that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: I see. Very good. And they allegedly had some kind of wooden rifles, as you say. Could you tell us, what colour were those rifles?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same colour as the wood, so dark wood.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Do you mean were they painted or was it just natural dark wood or something?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were not painted. It was like that natural dark wood.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Did they have these belts or something on them to carry them over the shoulder?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They kept them in their hands.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Could you -- since you've started describing the situation to us, could you tell us, what were they doing when you saw them? Were they standing, sitting down? Could you please describe the situation when you saw them? What were they doing, how were they at that moment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were sitting inside the room in a building as I described as Number 1 yesterday. They were sitting with the rest of us, all the other -- the soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: And these wooden rifles, where were they? Were they just next to them, in their hands, or what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: In their hands and on their laps, as you hold a rifle, as a hold a normal rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Did you perhaps see some crates with ammunition nearby, crates that would have to be taken to the front line? Did you see anything like that in that room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were at the front lines, so ammunition was tucked in magazines and pockets and bags over your shoulder, if any extra ammunition was being brought forward. I don't remember if I saw any cases of ammunition.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: And next to those prisoners, did you see anyone carrying them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Carrying what?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: No, no, no. Stretchers, did you see anyone carrying with stretchers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember I saw anyone carry any stretchers, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Tell me: At that moment when you saw them, did you know what those prisoners were supposed to do or what they were about to do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I knew that --

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: What?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew --

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: What were they to do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew they were to be used as a shield in front of our unit when we start the attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: How did you know that? Did somebody tell you that, explain it to you there on the spot, or had you learned it before -- a day or two before during the conversation that you had? How did you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was being told at the conversation a couple of days earlier when the plan was being told to us. And now they were there at the front line before the attack with wooden rifles, so it was obvious what they were being used as.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: All right. So my question was, you did not learn it there and then but from that previous conversation you have already described to us in detail. Thank you. Now, my question is, did anyone especially guard those prisoners? Was any kind of coercion applied to them? Were there any people with weapons surrounding them at that moment and guarding them until the moment when they were sent to the front line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I saw them, they were in this small room, the room we waited in while the artillery and the mortars were coming down. So in that room, there would possibly not be any way of escaping. And they were surrounded -- surrounded, you could say -- next to all of these soldiers, including me, with weapons, yeah, rifles.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: If I understand your answer, they were practically in the same situation as everyone else, except that you knew they were prisoners and those others were soldiers. Is that it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were in the same situation as the rest of us except their rifles were made from wood.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Of course. I meant -- what I meant was that there weren't any special guards guarding them, nobody else watched them, threatened them or -- I don't know -- forced them to do something, anything of that kind?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, you couldn't tell that by looking at the situation. But they were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Very well. Now, do you know, you personally, do you know what those men, those prisoners, were told? Prior to the action, do you know what they were told?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Do you know how they were picked out to take part? Why those men were selected to take part in the action?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how they were picked out. I heard from someone else - I don't remember who - that they were just put up on a line, and those three rifles were issued to three prisoners. How they were selected, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: You heard that, but you were not present, and you have no personal direct knowledge of that. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not present at that moment, no, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Do you know if that day, any one of those prisoners was killed or wounded? Of those three that you saw there, did you see any one of them killed that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not see anyone killed that day, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Do you know or did you learn later on if those prisoners, perhaps, fled to the side of the BiH army and stayed there on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you. This is only rumours that I heard after this attack, that one of the prisoners escaped over to the other side, the Muslim side. And also rumours that one was being killed, and one was still behind the Croatian lines. But as I said, it's only rumour that I heard. I can't tell -- can't say if it's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Very well. So my question was, did you know that that day they escaped and stayed there? And you say I heard various rumours, but you have no specific knowledge and personal knowledge. You have no personal knowledge whether they escaped. You did not see them or anything.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have no personal knowledge of what happened to these prisoners after this attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Very well. Now, we have this action underway. During the action, did you see those prisoners again; and if you did, tell us, please, where were they, what they were doing, what you were doing, how far you were from them. Will you please describe to us the situation when you saw them, if you saw them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw them inside this room where we were waiting while the mortars were coming in. And then the tank came out, started shooting, and the orders were given to attack. And those three prisoners were the first to run out in front of us. I saw that. But after that, when the enemy fire were coming in on us, I lost eye contact with them. After that, I don't know what -- where they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: All right. If I understood your answer, throughout this action, you saw them once at the moment when they ran out in front of everybody else, and that was the very beginning of the action. After that, you did not see them again. Is that what you said? Did I understand you well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Very well. Now, you said that in your view, they were to serve as a human shield. Will you please define the term "human shield" to us? Will you tell us what do you think their role was, if they were a human shield? What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would mean their role would be to take the first casualties, if there was to be any. The first enemy bullets would hit them instead of the rest of us. That would be their role.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Does that mean that they would protect you, shield you, with their bodies? Is that what it means?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Now, in that situation that you are describing to us, the three of them are running. I do not see them shielding anyone. How can they shield anyone with their bodies? Are you also running? Are you moving in a column? How are you moving? If they were to shield anyone with their bodies, how you were behind them, running, how are you moving?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: First, when we ran out of this little room where we had been waiting, we ran in a kind of single column until we came out in the open, and we spread out, mostly to the left side with the front to the enemy. We spread out to the left side along this low concrete wall in front of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Please, perhaps it will be easier if you show it to us on this map here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the usher please help me. This is 14/5, Prosecution's Exhibit. We saw it yesterday. So could we have it on the ELMO but with a clean copy, that is, an unmarked copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: So, Witness Q, you are familiar with this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Now, I should like to ask you to first show to us, and then -- and after that, we can also mark it. Can we see here, can you describe to us that moment when you saw those prisoners taking part in the action. So what we want you to tell us is, We were here when the attack commenced. I started to run. I saw prisoners there. And then let us try to see how did they shield you with their bodies. Perhaps we should start with this: Where were you before the attack started? Can you show it to us on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Over here in this building at the bottom floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Let's put number 1 here. Will you mark it straight away so that we can get a clear picture.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: This building, number 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: So you were sitting together there with the prisoners; I mean before the attack. And where did you then run out? Will you mark with number 2, the exact spot when you saw them. That is, you say they ran out, and I spotted them. So will you put number 2 at the place where you -- when you spotted them, when you saw them.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already saw them in the building, and then when the order --

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Yes, right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then the tank was starting shooting, and the orders to attack were given, and I saw them run out from this room.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: No, no, don't put anything yet. So you are saying that you were in the room when they were outside. Is that it, that you were inside and they were outside? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we were all in the room together.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Yes, I understand that. But when the attack started, you all left the room. Did you all leave at the same time, or did they come out first and you followed? Or did you stay behind in the room, and they were already out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the order was given to attack, they were the first sent out -- they were the first to run out, the three prisoners. And the rest of us, we followed them behind them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Now, will you put number 2 to mark the place where you saw them outside the building.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: There.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Now will you point at the direction or the road or the route which the tank was taking? You don't have to draw anything. Will you just point at it with a pointer? What was the route of the tank?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: The tank was -- the tank was coming from here, driving up on the side of the building next to us, right here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Right. So tell us, was there some connection between them and the tank; that is, was the tank pursuing some other task and they had nothing to do with the tank or was there something to do with the tank, between them and the tank? Or perhaps you can't tell us whether their actions were associated in any way with the tank.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: The tank was there to support us and the prisoners, and the rest of us were running between the tank and between Building Number 1. The tank had relation to us. It was there to support us, support the attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Right. Can you remember if there was any gunfire at the moment when those prisoners ran out? Was there any gunfire from any side at that moment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think there was a little gunfire, yes. But the gunfire started for real when we came out in the open, the open area.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Please, where did this fire come from? Were you protected? From which direction did this gunfire come? If we look at this mark 2, site number 2, where did the gunfire come from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I guess -- I'm not sure, but I guess it would -- from over here. No, wait.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: How far was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I guess about 75 metres or something.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: And were there any sandbags at this point marked "2"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a bunker nearby mark 2, sandbag bunker.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: And I guess -- aha, a bunker with sandbags. So that tank then moved forward. You drew to us its route yesterday. I'm asking you: On these streets here, were there any anti-tank protection? Were there anti-tank mines laid, were there those hedgehogs to stop the tanks? Was there any kind of protection here along this front line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there was -- there wasn't any tank protection, nothing. I don't remember -- I don't recall so.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: And to finish with this tank: How many projectiles did it fire, what was its role, how did it act?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: The tank acted like it was herding here, taking cover somehow behind the building, and once in a while it was driving up in the open, take aim and fire on enemy position. And I don't know how many rounds it fired up; 10, 15 rounds with the cannon.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: All right. Now, let's go back to the prisoners. Tell us, please, did these three prisoners shield you personally in any way? You say it was human shields, so were they a kind of a human shield for you, personally, under these circumstances?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I guess they were, they were human shields even for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: How did they shield you? Will you please explain it to me? I'm afraid I don't understand it. You explained to me what "human shield" means, and you explained it now. In real life, in the real situation, did they protect you in some way, and how? Will you please tell me, how did they protect you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were protecting me and protecting the rest of us, all the -- all of us, with their human bodies put between us and the enemy fire. That's just about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: How many of you were in that group; 10, 20?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's hard to tell, but I would say 15, 20, something about like that in this attack group. The rest of the unit was standing and supporting from the windows.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: And how far ahead of you were they? Are you moving in a single file, in a column, or are you all fanning out and running to take up your positions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, when we left the room, we ran in kind of a single column because it was a very narrow -- there was a very narrow space between the building and the tank and also the bunker. When we got out in the open area, we spread out. First in single column, and then we spread out on the line.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I see it is almost 11.00, and perhaps this will be a convenient time. I've covered more than half of the ground that I intended to cover, so perhaps this would be a convenient time to make a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We are adjourned until 11.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Par, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Witness Q. Can we now, please, have the map placed on the ELMO again. Witness Q, I would like to finish dealing with this map, and I would like to fill in some more details. Point 1 is the structure where you were before the attack. With "2", you marked the location where you saw these prisoners. Can you now mark with number 3 where the tank was, the tank that you mentioned, where that tank was. The point where you saw the prisoners, where was the tank? Am I to understand that the tank had passed through, and you and the prisoners came running out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true. The tanks were approximately at mark 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Very well. Can you now mark the positions of the AbiH. Maybe just draw one line and mark it with number 4.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Will you please repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: I would like you to mark the positions of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, that is the Muslim side. And if it is a longer line, maybe just draw a full line marking those positions.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll try to. Something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Very well. Can you now put numeral 4 somewhere along that line so that we know that these were the positions of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, or ABiH?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't exactly mark each enemy position because they were well concealed, camouflaged within these buildings. But the position were on or behind or maybe slight forward this line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Par. Mr. Par, before you continue, would you please give us some descriptions of those lines that the witness marked for the sake of the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course, Your Honours. Very well. Very well. For the record, witness, when asked to point the direction where the positions of AbiH were, drew a line along the Bulevar across from the building marked with number 1 where the witness was before the attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Witness Q, I understand your problem, but I am not asking you to mark specific positions of the members of AbiH. I would like you to simply mark with number 4 any part of the line that you drew, so just put it anywhere along the line, and we will simply know that that is to mark the line alongside which the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina was deployed, or where the line of defence or line held by the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina was. In other words, just put number 4 anywhere along that line.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay, understood.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Now, if I can ask you to, again, draw another line that would show where you believed yourself to be threatened by the enemy fire as you emerged from the building, in other words, where you thought you could have been fired upon and your lives could have been threatened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean from where?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Yes, the enemy positions.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: That could have been from anywhere, but I presume...

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: And perhaps you can put an arrow there, an arrow pointing towards number 1. If you can mark it with 5, next to the arrow. Now, will you please mark with the next number, 6, the low wall which you used as a cover when you emerged from the building. Now, can we, if at all possible, draw a line where that column was moving, the direction in which this column was moving so that we can see what space was covered between the building and the wall.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the route of the single column before we spread out on line, when we emerged from the building?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Can you tell us approximately what distance that was, how many metres from where you came out of the building to where you took cover?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Twenty-five, thirty metres, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: And do you believe that that was the space where you could have been threatened by the enemy fire before you took cover?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean if we were exposed to enemy fire before we took cover?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Well, going back to those human shields which you mentioned, my question to you is: Because your testimony, your evidence, was that there were two or three prisoners in front of you and there was danger of your being hit by enemy fire, this distance of 25 to 30 metres, was that the distance where you felt that you were in danger and where these human shields were supposed to help protect you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: The real danger started, I think, as soon as we spread out, just before we took cover below this low wall. I don't know whether there was any specific danger and why we were running in single column, but, yeah, there were bullets in the air and enemy fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Very well, thank you. Now, let me ask you one more thing concerning that column. Do you recall who was immediately ahead of you in that single column? Was that one of the prisoners or one of the members of the unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't exactly recall. But I was just about in the middle of this column, so it must have been a soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Thank you. Very well. Now, let me ask you one more thing for the record, because I probably did not say everything that you have drawn on the map. Can I also help you go down the list of the numbers that you've made? On Photograph 14.5, number 1 represents what, the building where you were before the attack started and which is on the boulevard behind the fountain; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Number 2 on this map is to the left of Structure 1, and it marks Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. the place where you saw the prisoners during this action; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the last place I saw the prisoners, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Number 3 marks the position of the tank at the moment when you came out, and its location is several dozen metres in front of the position marked with number 2; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was number 3's -- it's one of the points where the tank was, but you have to understand that the tank was sometimes taking cover behind the building and sometimes driving forward to aim and fire and reposition. So it was like driving backwards and forwards all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: I understand that. But just for the record, we're just trying to figure out what number marks what. So number 4 marks the line held by the AbiH forces, and it extends along the boulevard; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Point 5 is an arrow which marks a possible direction of fire from the enemy positions towards you, and it extends from the positions held by the AbiH forces at the boulevard towards a building marked with number 1. Excuse me for a moment. I'm not sure if we've covered all the points. Is there a Point 7? If we can keep this photograph there for a little while longer, can you give me an answer to this: From the positions which we marked as "4," along that line, were there any other positions from which you could expect fire, from which you were potentially threatened by enemy fire?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Very well. If you don't know, fine. Another question which is a follow-up question, but whether there were any Apex barriers or any other type of barriers that were deployed there. And do you recall any other incident -- another incident during your stay with Stela's unit when a car bomb was sent from the positions of AbiH? A small Fiat 750 model, this small vehicle was sent in the direction of your position, and can you tell us what stopped this vehicle? Were there any obstacles which prevented this vehicle from reaching your lines and killing you? Do you recall an incident like that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember the car bomb was stopped at our position, but I wasn't present at the front line that day. I arrived at the front line the day after. And what stopped this car bomb, I don't know if it was obstacles or friendly fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Very well, thank you. Just one more question concerning the prisoners. Where were those rifles when they stepped out of the building? When you saw them at the position marked with 2, did they have those rifles in their hands?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so, yeah. I'm not sure, but I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: You're not sure? Very well. That day, were you under influence of alcohol, drugs or anything else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Who was commanding this -- on that day in the course of this action?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Who was in command? I can't tell you for sure. There was a guy with a radio, giving orders. As I said before, it was hard to tell the structure of the unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Very well. You said that. But did you understand the language that he was speaking? Did you understand what orders he was issuing, what he was saying to whom at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was just sitting waiting for the attack. And when the orders was given, it was go, go, go. And it's pretty obvious what meant "go;" attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Witness Q, can you explain to us briefly, why did you ask for protection of this Court? What do you fear? What consequences might you suffer in your country as a result of your giving evidence here?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't want my names to be put out on newspapers, things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Very well. Do the police authorities in your country know of your appearing here to give evidence? Were they involved in making arrangements for your coming here or something like that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they are aware I was going down here. But all the arrangements was made from here, from the witness assistance --

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Very well, thank you. I'll take you back quickly to the units and to the events which you described while you were there. You said that on one occasion, foreign mercenaries who were German went to loot and told you about it. Did you see the looted goods?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Did they tell you to which neighbourhood they had gone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Did they tell you, were they looting abandoned apartments or apartments that were occupied by people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: The apartments were not abandoned. There were still people living in them, as I understood it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Very well. Did they describe to you the manner in which they committed these acts of looting? How did they loot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: They didn't speak to me especially about it, just that they were out in some neighbourhood where there were still living people.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: On that occasion, was this person, Adolf, under the influence of drugs or something else when he was telling you this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible. He had a --

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Very well, just briefly. And this Carlos, was he also inebriated or something like that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: This Carlos, he wasn't the man which drank alcohol or used drugs, anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Can you tell me, what does ethnic cleansing mean to you? Since you mentioned it yesterday, when you refer to ethnic cleansing, what do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whether it's ethnic cleansing or not, it's not up to me to decide. But I would describe ethnic cleansing as --

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I did not ask you to give me a definition. But when you say ethnic cleansing, what do you refer to when you say this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: To -- how should I describe? To get rid of some person that you don't want to be in the area, either by move them or kill them or just remove them from the area you don't want them to be in. That is what I would describe as ethnic cleansing, to remove a person that you don't want to be in --

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: And who are the persons -- I mean what are the criteria, who are the persons that we want in a certain area or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's probably the enemy population you don't want in the area, Serbs or the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Very well. You also said that you saw groups of elderly Muslims who were crossing the line of separation. And my question to you is, do you know why these people were crossing over to the other side? Were they driven out, or did they want to be in a part of town where the majority of their group was during this conflict?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if they were forced to go to the east part of the town or they volunteered to go to the east part. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Do you know that an identical situation was created on the other side, that numbers of Croats were crossing over to the other side of town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that people, Muslims, came to a unit every day, asking to be allowed to cross over to the other side to join their family, to move to another environment? They came to the unit to ask for help. Are you aware of those cases?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Right. Witness Q, did you ever have any contact of any kind with members of AID, Bosniak Security Service, at any time and on any matter before now, during your stay here?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean by "Bosnia Security Service"?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: The Bosniak Security Service, well, the Bosnian police, in a word. But this is a special one, this is a state police or a secret police, if you like, which performed certain affairs concerning witnesses. That's why I'm asking you. Did you have any contact with them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have no contact with any authorities from Bosnia or Croatia since I left.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this was the end of my cross-examination. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any re-examination, Mr. Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I've got a couple of questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Just to return to this incident with civilians being taken across the confrontation line, Witness Q, perhaps you will be able just to mark on the picture the place from where you observed that situation and the way the people were crossing the confrontation line. Could you do that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Just a moment. Don't touch upon the Defence exhibits.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Maybe the usher could put our own exhibit from yesterday, just P15.5/4, "/4" because it was marked by four witnesses. It's yesterday's.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Yes. And we'll put Number 4 here the way -- okay, could you explain now number 4?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. They were sent --

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Where were you at --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, for the Prosecutor. Please, microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Where were you at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in this position here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: "This position here," it means --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a bunker, there was a bunker here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Just for the record, Witness, put number "4" at the position of the bunker where you were.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Number 4 is put just next to the building identified as number 1. And where were the people coming from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were coming from behind this building, in between these two buildings, and sent this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: For the record, the witness is -- according to Witness Q, the people were taken from behind the building marked as number 3, just turning along the road, along the street.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: And here you may put "number 5" in the area of the arrow.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Next to the arrow?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Next to the arrow, yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Were those people escorted by some soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, they were. Before they were sent out, there was shouting from the Croatian side, "Don't shoot, don't shoot," in Croatian "Ne Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. pucaj," and they were sent out into the open. They were escorted, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: By whom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: By Croatian soldiers from the unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Was there firing in the area at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not heavy fire, but sporadic fire, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Thank you. My next question is: Yesterday, you identified in the courtroom a person whose nickname is "Stela". Do you know his real first name, full name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I later learned that it was Vinko Martinovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: And my last question is: Do you know if there was any investigation of the incident with wooden rifles and prisoners being used as human shields within the unit or on the HVO side?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whether -- if I knew there was some investigation?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's what my question is.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Okay. That is the end of my redirect, and I would like to tender into evidence our Exhibit 14.5/4. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Par.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, on behalf of the Defence, I should also like to tender this photograph, 14/5. Could we get a number, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The Defence number will be D2/5.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Judge Clark would like to ask a question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Witness Q, at the very early part of your direct examination, your "examination-in-chief" I think is what it's called here, you said that when you came to Mostar for the first time and you met Stela, that he was very suspicious of you and the other foreigners, and that he interviewed you and he was unwilling to take you. My understanding is that you said after that that he didn't really want to take you but he had to. Am I correct in that?
