utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's the way I understood it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: When you say "had to," do you mean that he was obliged to take you because he was short of soldiers or that there was a superior order?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course there was a superior order. That's what I mean.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: And why did you get that impression or how did you get that impression?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because we were sent from the headquarter in Mostar. Like the headquarter in Mostar decided where to put us, and that he was just ordered to take us in his unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: So is it your evidence that the decision as to which unit you were to go to, that was Stela's unit, was made at headquarters in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the impression I have of the situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: One very difficult question which I regret to say neither the Prosecution nor the Defence asked you, and obviously it's very important in this case: Were the prisoners that you refer to as "human shields" with the wooden guns, were they aware of the role they had to play in that attack? Did anybody tell them? Did they give any indication to you that they were aware?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think they knew. I don't know whether they have been told or not, but when we were sitting in this room in Building Number 1, waiting for the attack, it was obvious what they were being used as, and they looked very afraid.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: And is that something that you observed yourself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Judge Diarra, you have a question to ask?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DIARRA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. You spoke about a great lack of discipline and that there was disorder in Mostar. Do you mean that the orders would come from several people or that the soldiers simply were not obeying the orders? What did you mean when you said that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean it was hard to see any discipline or any structure as in a normal army, as I was used to. There, you would always have a structure with groups, platoons, companies, and each man know his role. And sometimes it was very hard to tell which role you played in this unit. And people seemed very undisciplined compared to normal armies, what I was used to as a soldier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DIARRA
utterances.text: Thank you. You also spoke about the building of bridges with sandbags. Was that work carried out only by military people, or were civilian prisoners used? Or was it only the civilian prisoners who built the sand bridges, that is, the bridges that were made with the sandbags?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: If there was to be put up any sandbags in windows or any places exposed to enemy fire, it was always prisoners being used, at least, that's what I saw; prisoner being used and guarded by soldiers with weapons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DIARRA
utterances.text: My third and final question is the following: You spoke about attacks. At the time of those attacks, were the soldiers being protected by civilian prisoners who were put in between you and the enemy fire? And during the attacks, were there any civilian -- did any of the civilian prisoners get killed or wounded? And if they were wounded, what happened to them afterwards? Were they then taken to be treated, or were they simply left there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never saw any prisoners being hit or wounded, anything. As soon as we came out in the open area, I lost eye contact with the prisoners. I was only thinking about the enemy positions and finding cover and shoot back. I lost eye contact with the prisoners, so I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DIARRA
utterances.text: I'm afraid I didn't understand your answer from the point when the prisoners were put in between you and the fire that was threatening you. You could know what happened to them. Did they fall? I didn't really understand what you answered.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if any prisoners were being hit. I didn't saw that. I lost eye contact with those prisoners. I didn't saw what happened to them. That's it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DIARRA
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Thank you, Mr. President. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any questions out of the Judges' questions from both sides?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, thank you very much. I have no questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honours, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, thank you very much for giving evidence. You may leave now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: As for the tendering of the documents, this Trial Chamber noticed that at the first day of the proceedings, the Defence counsel for Mr. Naletilic and Martinovic expressed their views. They have no objections to all those maps, photos, and the videotapes which compose in the binder Volume 1, from P1 to P53. In this case, they are admitted into the evidence, and the Registrar will give each proper number at a later stage. Thank you. Before we have next witness, I have something to seek to clarification from Mr. Krsnik. Mr. Krsnik, I would like to come to your motion to permit investigator to follow the proceedings filed on 10th of September, 2001. The Chamber has inquired with Registrar as to the legal status of Ms. Visnja Lasan and has been informed that after Ms. Visnja Lasan was substituted as co-counsel by Mr. Meek upon your request, she has not been assigned to the Defence team in any position. The Registrar has confirmed with the Trial Chamber that the legal status of Ms. Lasan as a potential member of the Defence team is currently under consideration and has not yet been decided upon. The Trial Chamber was further informed the Defence of Mr. Naletilic applied to have her assigned as a legal assistant while, at the same time, your motion was pending before the Chamber to have her present in the courtroom as an investigator. In addition, Ms. Lasan's special function as either a legal assistant or an investigator has to be established to follow the rulings by this Trial Chamber. In the meantime, the Trial Chamber will stay its consideration of your motion and request that you furnish further information upon the legal status of Ms. Lasan. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With your leave, Your Honour, maybe there is a certain confusion or misunderstanding here. So with your leave, I would like to explain that in August this year, as soon as we made a change of co-counsel, it was in our same motion that we suggested that Mrs. Lasan be designated as our legal advisor. That was in the first motion. And throughout, we have been moving to have her approved as the legal assistant, as the legal advisor. Her role on the team has been very important from the very beginning. She has been providing us with legal advice from the very beginning. And the Defence has problems, with which I do not wish to tax your patience, but we have had these problems from the very first day that we have come to this Tribunal. Our correspondence with the Registrar, we always have to -- we have to wait for the responses, and then we are requested to supply additional explanations. Mrs. Lasan is very important for the Defence team. So, Your Honours, you know that we have performed all the previous consultations and preparations and we gauged that this was very serious work. Because co-counsel is approved only two months before the hearing; before that, we are not entitled to a co-counsel. And because of that, because of this prohibition, we had to wait for that. Mr. Meek had other commitments elsewhere, in the United States. We had to wait for him to finish his business there. And as soon as we learned that the main hearing would start on the 10th of September -- and we knew nothing about that official until the 15th or the 20th of August, Mr. President, Your Honours, we did not know when the main hearing would start. But as soon as we learned it, then we informed the -- this Court and the Registrar of the change. Now, it was ten days ago already. We need her. She is indispensable to us in this courtroom, and I would appreciate it very much if you ruled to allow our legal assistant to be present in the courtroom. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I quite agree with you. There is some confusions and misunderstandings between us, and I request you to further any informations concerning the status of Ms. Lasan in a written form. Before that, we will stay the consideration of your motion. Thank you. So, who will take the next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President and Your Honours. I'll be taking the next witness. He is requesting pseudonym and facial distortion, so it may require a little bit of adjusting in the courtroom in order to bring him in. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Of course, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I believe the next pseudonym is the letter R, and so we have already written out the piece of paper with the witness's name and that pseudonym on it, which we can show him after he is brought in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are you fixing the -- and I hope you can have it copied and provided not only with the Chamber, but also with the Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, just so I'm clear, you would like that to be distributed prior to the time the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Before, before that witness is brought into the room.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: We will do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, maybe we could go to the private session for a while.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Now we are in the open session. Witness, would you please stand up and make the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Sit down, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness. The usher is going to hand you a piece of paper.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Good morning. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness, the usher is going to hand you a piece of paper. I'm going to ask you to look at it. Open it up and tell us whether inside you see your name, your date of birth, and also the profession or the job which you held during the years 1991, '92 and '93.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Yes, this is all correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: This paper will be admitted into evidence under the seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The number for this is W18.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Good morning, Witness. Just to inform you that -- can you hear me well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Yes, I hear you very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Just to inform you that for purposes of your testimony in these proceedings this morning, you have been given a pseudonym with the letter R, and I'll be referring -- all of us will be referring to you as "Witness R."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And let me ask you, while you are testifying, if you can keep in mind that you are protected, the Trial Chamber has granted certain protective measures in respect of your testimony so that if you could try to keep in mind not to tell us or not to say information which would identify you, such as what was your profession, or perhaps the names of other persons whom you were travelling with at various times.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: I've understood.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, Witness R, let me ask you whether generally speaking you travelled into the territory of the former Yugoslavia at various times during the years 1991, 1992, and 1993.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And if you could just give the Trial Chamber a little bit of background, some of the places in the former Yugoslavia that you went to during 1991, during the first part of the conflict there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: First I went to Slovenia. And then at the start of the war, I worked a lot in Eastern Slavonia. And then I went to Bosnia. In the meantime, I went back to the front in Dubrovnik in Central Bosnia, then Mostar, Livno, and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So in 1991, you mentioned Eastern Slovenia. Is that in the area of Vukovar, and were hostilities taking place in that region at the time you were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, in Vukovar and in Osijek.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And then you mentioned Bosnia in 1991. Were these the certain northern areas of Bosnia that you went to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. Bosanski Brod, Derventa.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: During those first trips to the former Yugoslavia, did you have an opportunity to observe various military groups and military operations which were taking place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, I would like to direct your attention, now, to late 1992, particularly the month of November, and ask you whether you and some of your colleagues made a trip into Central Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, please, precisely where did you go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: I think that the first time, it was the Travnik sector, specifically Novi Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And do you recall approximately the date in November '92 when you arrived in Novi Travnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: It was in November. I don't remember the exact date, but it was in November.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Was there a particular reason why you went to this place, Novi Travnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: We had learned that there was an initial clash between Bosnian Croats and Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And then if you can recall, what time of day -- what was happening in Novi Travnik when you arrived there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Well, it was kind of late in the evening, might have been 10 or 11. It was night, it was dark, there was fog. We were looking for a place to spend the night. And we stopped at the Novi Travnik Hotel, which is, in fact, in Novi Travnik. We stayed there, because in front of the hotel, there were military vehicles, Croatian vehicles. And so we stopped there to have some information and to spend the night.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, at this time I'm going to ask that the witness be shown Exhibit Number 3, which is one of the maps that has been tendered previously, a map of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And just to give us some idea, Witness R, with that map, can you indicate on the ELMO the location of Novi Travnik and Travnik also, another place that you have mentioned already. Perhaps using the pointer, you can point to the map the place that we're talking about.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: I don't see it very clearly here. Here.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. And now, just so we have something in the record, could you point to that place again, Novi Travnik. Okay. Thank you. Now, this is a place, for the record, that is a municipality located just to the west of another municipality called Vitez, and just to the northeast of a municipality called Bugojno. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: We're going to be talking about Travnik in a couple of minutes. So could you also indicate the location of Travnik, particularly the town or the city of Travnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Travnik is right here.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. And again, for the record, we are looking at a municipality located directly west of the Zenica municipality and east of the municipality of Jajce. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you. We can put the map away now. Now, coming back to your arrival, then, that evening in Novi Travnik, you pulled up to the hotel in Novi Travnik. If you could just briefly tell us, then, what did you see, what did you find upon entering that hotel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: The hotel was being occupied by HVO military personnel. We asked for a room, and it wasn't possible to have one. We asked whether we could have dinner, and they said that we could. So I said that we'll go to the restaurant, and it was filled with HVO military people. We had dinner there. And then we tried to find some information about the situation on site from people who we thought were military people, HVO military people, who would know something.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: During, then, the course of that dinner, did you and your colleagues, in fact, meet or speak with any of the HVO military personnel whom you found in the hotel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Can you tell us about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I was going to ask you if you could tell us about that, who were the individuals that you spoke to, or did you subsequently learn any of the -- meet any of those individuals whom you spoke to that night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Mr. Naletilic, among others, and then some military people whose names I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Someone, Ivan Soldo, who was one of Naletilic's deputies.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: That's sufficient. When you met, could you just tell us the circumstances of your meeting Mr. Naletilic. What was he doing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: His unit, I think it was his unit, or at least the unit where he was, had come up from Mostar, from Siroki Brijeg, more specifically because there was the first exchange of gunfire, first fighting with the Muslims. That had been the day before we arrived. And so the role of that HVO unit was to protect the Croats, any excesses on the part of the Muslim forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Let me ask you, again, before we talk in more detail about some of those matters, what was Mr. Naletilic doing when you first met him? How did you meet him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: What was he doing? He was having dinner. He was about 5 or 10 metres from the table I was at with other HVO military people.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, was there someone in your group, the people that you had come with, someone in that group who was able to speak or communicate with Mr. Naletilic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Yes, there was a colleague who speaks German. And so we were able to have some conversation with Mr. Naletilic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. So just so we're clear, then, the conversation that you had with Mr. Naletilic on that evening, this is conversation in German between him and one of your colleagues. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Yes, for the most part, mostly it was in German. There were a few words in Italian and French. But the conversation actually took place 90 percent in German.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So your recollection of what Mr. Naletilic said on that evening, does that come from what you were informed by your colleagues who spoke German?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right. Now, with that, bearing that in mind, then, could you just tell us what you learned that night? Who was Naletilic, what was he doing in Novi Travnik, what was happening there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: As I said to you, that HVO unit was at the Novi Travnik Hotel, and it had come up from Siroki Brijeg after the attack on the HVO headquarters in Novi Travnik carried out by the Muslim forces. So the HVO unit which was in the hotel had come as reinforcements and to protect the Croatian population.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: What did Mr. Naletilic indicate was his position in respect of these HVO soldiers --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: That's a very leading question. Pose it another way.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did Mr. Naletilic indicate whether he had any position --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: That's another leading question. Did Mr. Naletilic describe his position.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: On that evening, did Mr. Naletilic describe his position?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: No, not at all. Absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: On that evening, based on what you observed, the way he was treated by others, did you, in your own mind, determine whether he had any position?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, yes, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: If it please the Trial Chamber, that is also a leading question. I have to object to that. Suggesting the answer to the witness is highly inappropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: The question is, On that evening, based on what you Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. observed, the way he was treated by others, did you, in your own mind, determine whether he had any position. Maybe you could rephrase this question. Just directly ask the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I apologise, because I'm trying to be direct. I'm not doing a very good job.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: I think it would be very much simpler if you made shorter questions, if you said, "Did you observe anything about the group?" and lead on from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I think for the moment I'm just going to skip that question and come back to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So Witness R, tell us, how long did you and your colleagues, then, stay in this place, Novi Travnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: We spent one night at the hotel. We stayed in Novi Travnik for two or three days.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: During those two or three days, did you have an opportunity to observe Naletilic and these soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: What were they doing in the area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: I think that that unit we were talking about was at the Hotel Novi Travnik. And it was actually part of the Turbe sector, that was the part of the front that was at Turbe, and so it was opposite the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Were you able to see where these soldiers were during the day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Not during the day. I would see them late afternoon or during the -- at night in the mountains.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did you go there by yourself to see them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: No. Croatian -- HVO Croatian military people would come with us, since we didn't know the way, we didn't know how to go. It was dark, and so we were taken in HVO vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I see it's a bit after 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Okay. There is one thing I would like to remind you, Witness. Please do not talk to anyone about this testimony during the break, including any members of your family, no matter if it is face to face or over the telephone.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll adjourn until 2.30. --- Luncheon recess taken at 1.03 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Stringer, please continue with your witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness R, before the lunch break you were talking about some days you spent in Novi Travnik in November of 1992. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And you were talking about some soldiers that you encountered when you arrived at Novi Travnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you know what unit those soldiers belonged to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: No. I just knew that they were HVO soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: At any time during those days in Novi Travnik, did you learn who their commander was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: No, not during the time that I was in Novi Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So you don't know who was the commander of any of those soldiers?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: If it please the Court, if it please the Trial Chamber, that question, I object, as it has been asked and answered, and it should not be asked again. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think Mr. Stringer is confirming the answer from this witness. Is that true, Mr. Stringer?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You're just confirming it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I'm just trying to make sure it's clear what the testimony is.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: You don't know who was the commander of those soldiers that you met in Novi Travnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: I wasn't aware.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, you indicated just before the break that these soldiers -- you indicated that there was a Serb front line in the area. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: How far from Novi Travnik was this front line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: The front at Turbe must have been about ten kilometres away.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And did you go to that front line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: I went to that front line, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And were you allowed to go there just freely?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did anyone give you any authorisation to go there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Yes. We got authorisation from the HVO command, the Travnik sector or the Novi Travnik sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And I'm going to ask you about that in a few moments. Before, I want to limit, if you will -- first of all, let me ask you this: Soldiers that you saw in the hotel on that evening, were those soldiers deployed on this Serb front line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: You mean the same soldiers that I saw in the hotel and then on the front line? Well, I just don't remember. Really, I don't remember that, whether they were the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: You testified that on that first evening in Novi Travnik, you met someone named "Naletilic"; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And what was his position?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Really, at the time, I didn't know. We assumed -- my colleagues and I, we assumed that he was one of the officials there, but I don't really know on what level it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: What was the basis of that assumption?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Well, sort of he really had a kind of authority with the soldiers, and that made us assume that he was the one who was in charge of it. But we didn't know whether he was the person responsible.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, you indicated that you -- you mentioned the HVO command a few moments ago. I believe that was in Travnik.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: When did you go to Travnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Yes, I went there. You mean the HVO command?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: I think that it was the day afterwards. I think it was the day afterwards, after we spent the night at the Novi Travnik Hotel. The next day, we went to the command.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Who took you there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: We were with Mr. Naletilic and other HVO soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: What was the purpose of going there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: We wanted to go to the command in order to get a laissez-passer that would let us to go further into the zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Whom did you meet there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: I met several HVO officers. There must have been 10 or 15 people. I remember that General Blaskic was there. I don't know if at the time he was a general or whether he was only a colonel. But there was also Mr. Kordic. Among others. Those are the two people that I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: If you know, what was the position of General or Colonel Blaskic at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Well, I didn't know his rank, didn't know his rank. For him -- for me, he was either a general or colonel. I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: What was his responsibility, as far as you could tell?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: I assumed that he was the sector chief in Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Was Mr. Naletilic present when you met with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And just briefly, if you know, what was the title and the function of this person named Kordic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: He must have been in the HDZ in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, if you know, what was the HDZ?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: That was the opposition party to Tudjman.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: It was Tudjman's party. Excuse me. Interpreter's correction. It was Tudjman's party.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Just for clarification, was this a military organisation or some other organisation, HDZ?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: It was political organisation. It still is.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And were you given anything at this meeting with Mr. Blaskic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: I was given a laissez-passer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, at this time I'm going to ask that the witness be provided what has been marked as Exhibit P198.1. And I believe that copies have been circulated to the Defence, and I believe that the Registrar also has copies for Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are they in the binders we have here?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, they are not. These are additional.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness R, if you could take a look, it's two sheets of paper which has been placed in front of you. One is an interpretation. Can you describe what this document is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: I didn't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Could you just describe -- well, let me ask you this --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, this is a laissez-passer which was given by Colonel Tihomir Blaskic. It was issued by the operative zone in Central Bosnia, and it's dated 25 November 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Does this document bear the names of yourself and the other persons whom you were travelling with at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And with that document, then, how did you -- if you could tell us just briefly then, once you had that document, how did you use it, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: I used it or, rather, we used it, that is, the four journalists, in order to pass the different checkpoints and when we would come close to the front line. Of course, I'm talking about the HVO checkpoints.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if you know, what was the role of this person Naletilic in Novi Travnik at the time you met him there? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: I didn't know Mr. Naletilic at that time. I never heard him say his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: What was the role -- from what you observed, what was the role he played in Novi Travnik during that period of time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Hard to say, hard to say. Without question, he had responsibilities, but I don't know at what level they were and -- or Colonel Blaskic either.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, I believe you indicated that you spent two or three days there in that area of Travnik and Novi Travnik before leaving. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: That's correct. Excuse me. In the Novi Travnik sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I'm referring to. During that period of time, did Mr. Naletilic tell you where he came from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: During that period, yes, he told me that he came from Siroki Brijeg. And at that time, I didn't know where Siroki Brijeg was.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, you then left Novi Travnik, and this is presumably still in November. Subsequently at some point, did you travel to Siroki Brijeg?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Yes, a few months later.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what month it was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: I think that it was in the late spring, at the end of the spring, the beginning of the summer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: What was your purpose in going to Siroki Brijeg?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Mr. Naletilic had told us that if we were going to work in Mostar and we were going to go through Siroki Brijeg, we could come to see him and ask for his assistance, and that's what we did. At least that's what I did myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So at this time, then, had you decided in fact to work in Mostar or Siroki Brijeg?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Why had you decided to work in this area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: For a very practical reason. All the international press was concentrated in Sarajevo at that time, there were a great many journalists there; whereas in Mostar, it had been somewhat forsaken by the press, and I thought it might be interesting for me to concentrate especially on Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Had there been any developments in the Mostar area which drew your attention to that place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Yes. I had gone there a few months before, and I realised that there was already a degree of tension between the Croatian and Muslim ethnicities, and there were precursor signs of the clash that was about to come.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Prior to your arrival in the Mostar/Siroki Brijeg area, had there been any military activities between the Croats and the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Well, there had been the incidents in Novi Travnik, and also in Mostar I think that there was some problems. There was the attack on the Armija headquarters by the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Had that attack taken place before your arrival?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Before I arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Can you tell us approximately how long before you arrived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Just a few days before, because the buildings in which the headquarters were located still had smoke coming out of the windows, so it had really just happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, can you tell us what happened when you arrived in Siroki Brijeg?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: I asked to meet with Mr. Naletilic, and I was told that he wasn't there, that he was in Mostar. They had me wait about two or three hours right near the Park Hotel, and then around 4.00 or 5.00 that same day, someone came to get me and took me to Mr. Naletilic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Before someone came to take you to Mr. Naletilic, where did you spend those three or four hours, where did you wait for that to happen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: We were in an anti-aerial position that was behind the Park Hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, at this time I would ask the witness be shown Exhibit 26.11, which is a photograph. If we could put that on the ELMO, it might just speed things along, rather than everyone having to reach for it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, Witness R, looking at this photograph, can you tell us if you recognise the place that's shown in that photo.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Yes, that was the Hotel Park.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So this is the place that you've just mentioned as where you were waiting after you arrived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. We stayed in the anti-aerial shelter that was behind the hotel, and then we waited on the terrace right in front of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: At some time, did you ever learn what that shelter was used for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: No. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, you indicated that at some point, someone came to take you to Naletilic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you recall the name of the person who came to take you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: I think that it was Ivan Soldo.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I believe that earlier in your testimony you mentioned the name of Ivan Soldo in connection with the events in Novi Travnik.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Yes, I had seen him for the first time at the hotel, Novi Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And is it, then, the same person that came for you that day in Siroki Brijeg?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: When I was in Siroki Brijeg, you mean. Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, at this time I'm going to ask the witness be shown Exhibit 704, which is a document, and not necessarily for the ELMO. And I'm going to ask Witness R if he can simply turn to page 10 of the English translation, which he has in front of him. I can say for the record, this is not a document that he has seen before.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And I simply wanted to ask you, Witness R, if on page 10 of that document, you see the name of this person, Ivan Soldo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Indeed, the fifth one.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you. Okay, that's -- we can take that document. We're finished with it. Now, Witness R, when this person, Soldo, came for you, where did he then take you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: We went exactly to the villa of Mr. Naletilic, which was at Siroki Brijeg.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And who was present at the villa when you arrived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: There were several military and some civilians. I was represented to a elderly man, and I was told that he was a representative of Croats, either at the United Nations or in Canada. I believe in Canada.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Correction. Not United Nations. United States.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, at this time, I ask the witness be shown two photographs, Exhibits 25.5, 25.6. Place 25.5 on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness R, do you recognise the place that's shown in Exhibit 25.5?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Indeed I do. That is Mr. Naletilic's mansion.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And Exhibit 25.6, just briefly.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Yes. This is the same building, and it faces Siroki Brijeg. Siroki Brijeg is down there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, at this point, I would like to ask you some questions. First of all, did you go to that place which you've described as the residence of Mr. Naletilic? Did you go to that place on other occasions, beginning with this trip in May of 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: We have had the opportunity to go there, I believe it could have been 8 or maybe 12 times. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to ask you some questions about this period beginning in May, some general questions. First of all, during that period, did you live in this area or did you live elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: In the beginning, that is, the first time that I travelled there, in Mostar and Siroki Brijeg, I stayed there for a very short time. I met with Naletilic in the evening. He invited me to a dinner, but I had a meeting in Split. And I had to leave for Split around 9.00 in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did you return to this Mostar/Siroki Brijeg area subsequently in the months that followed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: How frequently did you return to that area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Well, once every 45 days.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: How long would you stay in the area when you came there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Well, it varied but, say, five or six days on the average. At times longer, at times less than that, because I used Siroki Brijeg as a place for which I could go to other places in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Why did you use Siroki Brijeg as a place from which you could go elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: In a way because it was near Mostar. It was interesting to follow the situation in Mostar at the time. It was a good place. And secondly, because from Siroki Brijeg or Mostar, I could go northward, that is to Central Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. And did these trips back to the Mostar area continue for the rest of 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And during these trips that you would make to Mostar and Siroki Brijeg, did you have the opportunity to meet and speak with Mr. Naletilic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Yes, several times.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: How did you communicate with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: It was rather difficult because I do not speak German, so at times there was somebody who could speak some English and they served as interpreter, or we managed with Italian and a sprinkling of French. Besides, I've lived in Italy, so that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, did you meet with Mr. Naletilic in places other than Siroki Brijeg?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: I met Mr. Naletilic once in Zagreb, once or twice, and I'd say that was all. Siroki Brijeg, Mostar, and one or two times in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Well, did Mr. Naletilic indicate what he was doing in Zagreb when you met him there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Yes, I suppose he had some meetings, some appointments, with political people, with people from the HDZ and from people with the Ministry of Defence, such as Mr. Susak in particular.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Who was Mr. Susak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: The Minister of Defence of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did you ever see him with Mr. Naletilic in Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Only once. I believe that it was during this accidental meeting at the Intercontinental Hotel. We were sitting at a table, sitting at a table, and Mr. Susak came. And Mr. Naletilic stood up to greet him, and they talked for about five minutes, and then Mr. Naletilic sat down again.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did you ever see Mr. Susak in Herzegovina, the area of Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Mostar/Siroki Brijeg?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: I did, yes, once at Siroki Brijeg.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Can you be a little more specific about where he was and what he was doing on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: I have no idea why Mr. Susak was visiting Siroki Brijeg. I saw him for about five minutes, and that was in the house of the mayor of Siroki Brijeg.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: What was Mr. Susak's role, if any, in Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: I think that Mr. Susak was very conversant with the situation in Bosnia-Herzegovina and interested in it, since he himself was a Herzegovinian.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did Susak possess any authorities in Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Could you repeat the question, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did Mr. Susak possess any authority in Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Formally, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Informally?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Most certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: What's the basis of your statement on that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: According to what the Croatian press had said.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And did you speak to anyone yourself on that subject?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Yes, with colleagues, foreign and Croatian, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you ever speak with Mr. Naletilic about his plans or goals in respect of this region, Mostar/Siroki Brijeg?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: During the conversations I had with Mr. Naletilic, these conversations were very limited in scope, for some mysterious reason. It was really very difficult to know what were Mr. Naletilic's plans. What I can -- well, he was defending the interests of the Croat community in Mostar. But as for his short-term or long-term plans in Herzegovina, I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you ever meet a person during this period named "Ivan Andabak"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Several times, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, who was that man, Ivan Andabak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: He was an officer in the HVO, recently promoted to general. I don't know what his rank was at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Where did he live?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: At Siroki Brijeg.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did you ever have any social dealings with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: I met him several times at Siroki Brijeg and in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did you ever have lunch with him and his wife?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Once, yes, went to his place and had lunch with him and his wife.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: What was his function or his role?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: I think that he was more or less responsible for the logistics of operations taking place elsewhere; that is, that he was responsible for supplies. Perhaps he had some other responsibilities. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Was he in charge of logistics for any particular military group or unit?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: May it please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Counsel Meek. Mr. Meek, microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I apologise. I thought I had put it on. I object to that question, as this witness has just answered that he does not know what Mr. Andabak's role was, and so the form of the question is improper.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Stringer, would you please clear up this issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, the witness said that he thought Mr. Andabak was responsible for supplies, logistics. I simply asked for what military group or unit. I don't know how I can ask it any more clearly. I think it's a proper question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Mr. Stringer, I think you have been leading rather a lot. And without objections from Defence, I have let you go. But you ought to know how to ask questions of an important and material witness. If you ask him the question following on the answer when he gives a partial answer, and then qualifies it by not knowing too much, the question you should put is, Do you know anything more about this?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I'll try to question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: You will appreciate that this is a material witness, and we must be fair to both sides. And you know how to ask questions, I suspect, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I do, indeed, appreciate that this is a material witness, Your Honour. And I will do my best.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: That's all we ask.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness R, do you know anything more about the role or the function of Mr. Andabak in addition to his role in a logistics capacity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: No, I think that is my opinion at all, that he was primarily an administrative role, administrative above all, and I think he dealt with logistical matters and personnel and things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you know what military unit he performed this function for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: From a moment on when he assumed command in Siroki Brijeg, it was for Naletilic's forces, you know, at Siroki Brijeg.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did you ever see Naletilic and Andabak together?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: What was the relationship between the two of them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Friendship, I would say.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I'm talking about professionally or militarily speaking.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: What was their relationship? I think that Mr. Andabak informed -- reported to Mr. Naletilic about the work done.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Have you ever heard of something called Kaznjenicka Bojna, or "Convicts' Battalion" in English?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Yes, Kaznjenicka Bojna.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: What was the Kaznjenicka Bojna?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: It was an HVO unit headquartered at Siroki Brijeg, and which then became known as the Diverzantski Odred.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Who was the commander of the Kaznjenicka Bojna?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Well, if I refer to what the press said, it was Mr. Naletilic. But I personally have no elements on which I could base this or some other conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, Witness R -- Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Let me just, Mr. President, ask if the witness could be shown Exhibit 262.1.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness R, again, this is two pages. One is a translation. Do you recognise this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Indeed. This is a pass issued by the HVO, and I was issued with it by the person responsible in the Mostar police, allowing me to move around Mostar. Unfortunately, there is no date.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, please, how you received this laissez-passer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: At the time, it was very difficult to move around Mostar because there were all sorts of checkpoints. And I asked Mr. Naletilic if it would be possible to have a laissez-passer to be able to enter Mostar, and who should I go to in order to resolve this formality. And Mr. Naletilic gave me a name, and it was the person who was the commander of the Mostar police, Mr. Jelic, that saw that I could go. He issued me with this, and I could go to Mostar owing to the recommendation of Mr. Naletilic. That is this pass which allowed me to move freely around the Croat part of Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: You mentioned that Mr. Naletilic gave you a name. Did he give you anything else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: No -- oh, yes, yes, yes. I think he spoke to somebody over the telephone, and I think that conversation had to do with this laissez-passer. And after that, he wrote down the name, which I didn't keep, but it was Mr. Jelic's name asking him -- that is, I went to him and was issued that laissez-passer pass.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And with this laissez-passer, were you able to move around certain areas in the region?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Yes, I could move around the Croat part, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Were there any areas in which you were not able to go? Within the Croat areas, were there any places where you could not go with the laissez-passer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: In Mostar?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: I could move freely practically all over except that I could not enter the airport area.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Have you ever heard of a place called the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Were you able to gain access to the Heliodrom with the laissez-passer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Heliodrom, I do not think -- I do not know whether I would be free to enter it because I never went there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did you ever -- during the time that you spent in the Mostar area, did you encounter any personnel or weapons of the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Yes. In that sector, as in other sectors, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: First of all, were these personnel or materiel that you are referring to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: As for the materiel, it is much more hard to say. As for the persons, yes, I saw various military from Croatia. And in the press, I saw also some of them came from the 4th Brigade in Split.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you ever go to a place called -- or meet -- I'll start over. Did you ever hear of something called the "ATG Vinko Skrobo"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Indeed, yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you know what the ATG Vinko Skrobo was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Well, it was an anti-terrorist group, but I think it was -- that was formally, but that was an HVO unit which was deployed in Mostar. There were several ATGs, as they were called at the time. Vinko Skrobo, I think, was a unit which was deployed at a place called "Rondo" in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did you ever go to this place, the Rondo in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Yes, on various occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Have you ever met a person called "Vinko Martinovic" or "Stela"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Yes, two or three times at least.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Roughly when did you meet that person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: The first time, I met him in the -- before the events that we are interested in. At the time, Mr. Martinovic was a member of the HOS, or at least when I met him he had an HOS uniform, but I didn't know who it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did you ever meet this person, Martinovic, in the area of the Rondo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And what was his function?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: I think that he was responsible or commander of that ATG that you mentioned earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, did you go to this location, ATG Vinko Skrobo, at any other time with any other people or persons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: I went twice to the command of that ATG. Yes, well, I met a number of people who were its members, but I didn't know them.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Was Stela present every time you went there? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Oh, no, not at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did you ever go there with any HVO or military personnel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: At times, yes. And at times when I would be in Mostar, when I was issued with this pass, who resolved all my problems with the military police or HVO units which were deployed on the ground, then no.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did you ever go there with Andabak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Once, yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: What was the purpose of that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: I couldn't answer that question. I was with Andabak on that day. We were walking around the -- making a tour of the front lines, and we went to that ATG.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Roughly, if you know, the general time frame in which you went there with Mr. Andabak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Well, it was in the fall, in the fall, a few weeks before the destruction of the Stari Most, the Old Bridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, Witness R, we've reached the end of your examination-in-chief, and at this time I'd like to ask you, if you would, to look around the courtroom and tell us if you see either of the persons that you've testified about, either Mr. Naletilic or Mr. Martinovic, in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: I see Mr. Naletilic, who is on the right, and Mr. Martinovic is to my left.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, may the record reflect that the witness has identified the accused. Thank you. Mr. President, no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Cross-examination. Defence counsel for Naletilic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Again I would like to ask of Mr. Usher to please lower the ELMO so that I can have a clear view of the witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Witness. I am the Defence counsel for the accused Mladen Naletilic, and I'm going to ask some questions of you, which I'm going to try to focus so as to make them as succinct as possible, due to the time that we have left and everything else. So I thank you in advance for your cooperation. Siroki Brijeg is a large city?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: No. No, it's a small town just west of Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Does it have more than 1.000 inhabitants? And I'm referring only to the town itself, not the whole municipality.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Well, you're asking me too much there. I think there were more than a thousand people, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: My apologies. I am just asking questions that I assumed you may be able to answer, so please don't get upset if I go too far in my assumptions.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Well, I could have asked the mayor of Siroki Brijeg for that information. I would have -- I must have asked him, in fact, but I don't remember what he answered.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: There's a reason why I ask you this question. This is cross-examination, and I was just trying to get to the main point. My main point is: Do you think that everybody in this town knew each other and sort of socialised?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Yes, I think so. I myself come from a small town. Everybody knows everybody.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: This is precisely the point that I was trying to make for the Trial Chamber. This is why we're here, in order to try to clarify matters so that we can arrive at the truth. Mr. Susak, about whom my learned colleague asked you in the examination-in-chief, was born in Siroki Brijeg. Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: His parents' house was there and also his own family house was built there. Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: That's what I was told, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: He went to school in Siroki Brijeg, including the secondary school. Did you also hear that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Yes, part of his studies were in fact done there in Siroki Brijeg.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did you hear about or did you know from personal knowledge that a number of persons like my client grew up together with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: I could imagine that would be the case, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did Mr. Susak come to visit his mother, his family, and to spend some holidays in his hometown, or did you hear about it? He would come in the summer or the winter for holidays?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Yes, I know that. I know all of that, yes. I was told.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So during his visits, during all his holidays and vacations, he met with his friends and acquaintances, talked to them in restaurants and in the Park Hotel. Did you see him walking around in town and talking to his friends?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President. I've just read the last question of counsel, which actually reads more like testimony to me, and I would simply ask if the questions could be a bit more like questions in nature, rather than statements about what any person did or didn't do in Siroki Brijeg. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, I think the question is okay, but you don't need to have a description of the situations before your question. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I will pay attention to that. But in cross-examination, I'm trying to frame a question in a wider way so that I can get a shorter answer, because this is cross-examination rather than examination-in-chief. But I do acknowledge your intervention, and I will make necessary adjustments.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Can you tell me, please, when exactly, if you recall, were you in the house where you met Mr. Naletilic -- or where you met Mr. Naletilic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: The first time?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yes, what year? And in Siroki Brijeg.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Well, I said to the Court it was at the beginning -- well, in the summer of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: My question is, for the record, you said 1992, but I'm more interested in 1993. Would you be able to recall the month? Was it April, May, June, July, if you can recall, in 1993 when you first came to that house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Must have been June or in July, but I'm not absolutely sure. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Was the house completed at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Most of the major work had been done, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Can you now tell me, please, when you were in Siroki Brijeg, how many different HVO units were there in Siroki Brijeg, if you know, deployed there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: In Siroki Brijeg, I really couldn't say. Aside from the unit in which Mr. Andabak was a member, I don't see any others. But it doesn't mean that there weren't any others.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Can you now please tell me, if you know, again, do you know what types of units were there? Were there small units? Were there any special-purpose units, the ones that you know of?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: I think you're speaking about the units there in Siroki Brijeg. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: As far as I know, I don't think there were other ones there, aside from the Convicts' Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence of Mr. Naletilic has checked all the facts that we care to check in our cross-examination. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Seric.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am Branko Seric, and I represent Mr. Vinko Martinovic. You said that you were -- you went to see one anti-terrorist unit with General Andabak. Can you tell us which unit that was, if you can recall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: It was Vinko something. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Could it have been Benko Penavic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: I know Benko Penavic. The problem, you see, is that there were several there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Let's cut it short. Was that unit under the command of Vinko Martinovic when you were there with General Andabak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: When we went with Mr. Andabak, we visited several command posts of the ATGs, and we also went to a command post which was under the responsibility of Mr. Naletilic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: You said that on several occasions, you went to Mostar. Did you go to coffee bars there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Were there armed soldiers there? Were there any incidents in those coffee bars?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: In all the Mostar cafes, the soldiers were armed, but I never saw any incident in the Mostar bars.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Again, if you can remember, on 8th, 9, and 10 August, you gave statements to the Tribunal investigators. Do you recall your statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: I remember, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that you said that the situation in the city was dangerous and that there was a prevailing atmosphere of civil war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Yes, I have a couple that I would like you to clarify if you can. I'm a little confused about all these names. Were any of the important people identified, Mr. Kordic -- I'm going to go through the names mentioned. When you met him, was he in uniform? What uniform was that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Witness, you have to answer the question in words, not in any body languages like nodding, for the sake of the record.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Mr. Kordic, Mr. Kordic was in a uniform -- well, he was in military fatigues. It didn't have any insignia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: I think you mentioned something about HDZ.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Yes, that's a political organisation, a political party, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: So if I understand you correctly, so Mr. Kordic, when you saw him, was in army fatigues without insignia. So you couldn't identify which army he belonged to? You have to say something.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Yes. That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Mr. Blaskic, was he in uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Mr. Blaskic was also in uniform. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Was that the same uniform without insignia, or could you identify to which army he belonged?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: He had HVO insignia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Mr. Naletilic, did you ever see him wearing military clothes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: I saw him in a fatigue jacket. I didn't really see him dressed head to foot in a military uniform.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: And again, was this a jacket without insignia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Sometimes he had insignia, and sometimes he didn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Could you identify the insignia when you saw it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: HVO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: HVO. And then we had the gentleman -- let me see -- Mr. Susak, who apparently is a native of this small town, whose name I dare not pronounce, who you described as the Minister of Defence for Croatia, the Croatian Republic, I take it, the separate country of Croatia. Mr. Susak, was he a military man or a civilian?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: He was a civilian. He was a minister.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: But I take it he never wore a uniform.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: I never saw him in a uniform.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Andabak, what was the situation in relation to Mr. Andabak, again, another native of Siroki Brijeg, I think?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: I think that he was from Siroki Brijeg.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Yes. That's what I understood the Defence cross-examination to indicate. Did he wear a uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: General Andabak? Yes, yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: And what uniform was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: That was green, with HVO insignia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: And the second accused in this case, Mr. Martinovic, when you met him in Mostar on the few occasions that you met him - and I think at the cafe and other places - did you ever see him in uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Yes, I saw him in uniform several times. Yes, I did. I'm sorry. I also saw him in civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: You described having lunch with him and his wife. Was that the same uniform as Mr. Andabak and --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: You're speaking about Mr. Martinovic or Mr. Andabak?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Mr. Martinovic. You said you saw him in uniform and in civilian clothes, and I was just asking you: Was the uniform that he wore similar in any way to the one worn by Mr. Andabak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Thank you. I just wanted to get the uniforms right. Just one last question. As you spent some time in Croatia, is the uniform of the official Croatian army significantly different from the HVO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: The uniforms of the HVO or the Armija people, all those uniforms, really very much alike, all of them. You really had to look very carefully at what insignia was being worn in order to know whether this was Croats from Croatia, or Croats from the HVO, or even Armija soldiers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: I understood you to say at one stage, in response to a question that was posed by Mr. Stringer for the Prosecution, that you saw Croatian army personnel in parts of Central Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: Yes, I saw him. I described him. It was described by other people who were with me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: And are you satisfied that you could make a distinction between the army personnel from the official army of Croatia from that of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: From the time that I asked the questions of the soldiers to find out what unit they were in, to say exactly what units they were in, at that point I could say whether they were from the HVO or from the Croatian army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: So you have no doubt about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS R
utterances.text: No, I have no doubt.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any questions out of Judge Clark's questions? Yes, Mr. Stringer.
